A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PQQA research, with readable text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. Retained material can be matched despite additions, relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original PQQA/QQA solution-quality, runtime and ablation results for maximum independent set, maximum clique and max cut in Section 5 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds PQQA experiments on balanced graph partitioning and graph coloring in Sections 5.4-5.5.

M1.justification: v1 specifies a binary procedure and mentions possible extensions. v2 specifies and evaluates a categorical adaptation using K-category probability vectors, generalized entropy and row-normalized clamp transformations (Appendices B and C.4). It also corrects the written binary entropy sign; this correction alone does not establish that the implementation changed.

E1.justification: Coverage expands from three binary graph problems to five tasks. v2 adds balanced partitioning of five neural-network computation graphs and coloring of twelve COLOR instances, introducing multicategory assignments and new task requirements. The previous benchmark coverage is retained.

E2.justification: New comparisons introduce hMETIS and GAP for partitioning (Table 5), and Tabucol, GNN, PI-GCN and PI-SAGE for coloring (Table 6). Existing comparator sets remain, including CRA-GNN in Table 2 despite its removal from the introductory baseline description.

E3.justification: The added evaluations introduce joint edge-cut/balanceness assessment and conflict minimization at specified color counts. For existing MIS and clique experiments, the stated penalty changes from 1.0001 to 2 (v1 Appendix C.1; v2 Appendix D.1). This is a reported setting revision, without evidence that the unchanged result tables were regenerated.

E4.justification: The SA comparison and schedule, initial-gamma and communication-strength ablations are retained. Appendix C.1 adds a qualitative report that sigmoid performs worse than clamp, but supplies no numerical comparison or experimental protocol for that additional analysis.

E5.justification: v2 explicitly identifies the ablation shading as standard deviation across five random seeds in Figure 3. The SA comparison also changes its description from mean and variance to mean and standard deviation. The existing five-seed RRG reporting remains; additional runs are not established.

E6.justification: Tables 5-6 add substantial new results: PQQA reports partition cut ratios of 0.03-0.04 with 0.99 balanceness, and 11 and 14 coloring conflicts on queen11-11 and queen13-13, versus PI-SAGE's 17 and 26. Existing benchmark scores are retained; these are new-task findings, not improvements over v1 under matched conditions.

T1.justification: Appendix B adds a generalized categorical entropy, formal discrete-variable relaxations, and Proposition B.1 proving recovery of the binary entropy when K=2. Section 3.2 corrects the binary entropy from the sum of (2p-1)^alpha-1 to the sum of 1-(2p-1)^alpha. The existing convergence theorem and Appendix A proofs remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The central claims of a competitive general-purpose solver and favorable large-instance speed-quality tradeoffs remain. v2 makes the general-discrete extension an explicit contribution rather than a prospective capability, while its conclusion redirects future work toward mixed-integer optimization and sampling.

C2.justification: Appendix C.1 adds a mechanism explanation linking sigmoid saturation to difficult transitions near discrete values. Section 5.6 emphasizes preserved quality with fast annealing, replacing v1's emphasis on schedule sensitivity despite retaining the curves. The partitioning discussion also acknowledges PQQA's runtime disadvantage against GAP alongside its cut-quality advantage.

D1.justification: v2 adds the explicit normalized-clamp transformation for categorical variables, coloring instance sizes and color counts, and partitioning graph statistics. It revises the documented MIS/clique penalties. Existing optimizer, temperature, annealing-schedule and V100 hardware disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting Gibbs sampling, partitioning and coloring, and removes Ciarella et al. (2023). Section 4 shifts criticism toward iSCO's approximation, tuning requirements and absent inter-chain communication. The alpha-entropy attribution also changes from Ichikawa et al. (2022) to Ichikawa (2023).

P1.justification: Extensive paragraph rewriting spans the abstract, introduction, background, method, related work, experimental discussion and conclusion. The experimental narrative now covers five tasks before ablations, and the appendices are reorganized around the added generalization and implementation discussion.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the displays with partitioning and coloring comparison tables, a coloring-statistics table and an expanded real-world dataset table. Existing plots are resized or relocated, tables gain metric-direction arrows and bold emphasis, and the Optsicom display changes from Figure 1 to Table 4. Retained curves are not new results.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the general-purpose claim by specifying and testing a categorical extension beyond v1's binary tasks. Correcting the entropy sign also resolves a central mismatch with the stated annealing behavior. These gains outweigh documentation weaknesses, although the new coloring objective in Eq. (29) has the opposite sign from the stated conflict-minimization goal, and the revised MIS/clique penalties remain unexplained.
